open_points.subject: AdmissionVerdict identity and repeated admission
open_points.text: “Substitution: a verdict for the same implementation and corpus is the same verdict.” / “every active case of the corpus is run again for the implementation at admission time, and the verdict covers exactly those executions.”
open_points.question: When the same implementation is submitted again against an unchanged corpus, is the existing verdict reused, or is a new verdict created for the newly minted TrialExecutions?
options: Reuse the existing verdict and do not run a new admission
Create a distinct verdict for each admission execution batch
Replace the prior verdict while retaining the new TrialExecutions
open_points.default_guess: Create a distinct verdict for each admission execution batch, because the text requires the cases to be run again and TrialExecutions are distinct observations.

open_points.subject: ProofResult identity
open_points.text: “Substitution: proving the same version gives the same result.” / “whether a flow version whose proof failed because a binding was not yet accepted can be proven again later — closed by A05 (yes).”
open_points.question: What identifies a ProofResult when the same immutable flow version can have different results as referenced bindings move from proposed to accepted?
options: ProofResult identity includes the relevant mutable dependency state
Each proof computation is a distinct observation
ProofResult has no durable identity because it is computed on demand
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as an on-demand result whose facts reflect dependency state at evaluation time, rather than as one invariant value per flow version.

open_points.subject: Accepting an already accepted binding without a selected service instance
open_points.text: “an accepted one is returned whatever the manifest says now” / “a binding for it is refused when proposed or accepted”
open_points.question: If an accepted binding's service currently has no selected instance, does another accept request return that binding or refuse the request?
options: Return the already accepted binding regardless of the missing instance
Refuse every accept request while the instance is missing
Refuse only acceptance of proposed bindings; return bindings already accepted
open_points.default_guess: Return bindings already accepted, while refusing acceptance of proposed bindings.

open_points.subject: Run status with both failures and waiting points
open_points.text: “its status is `awaiting_approval` when any of them waits for the owner's approval, otherwise `pending`” / “The run is `failed` when no node can run any more and some node failed”
open_points.question: When one branch has failed and all remaining unfinished branches are waiting, is the run still waiting or does it end as `failed`?
options: Waiting takes precedence until every waiting point is resolved
Failure takes precedence as soon as no node is runnable
Only particular waiting reasons prevent final failure
open_points.default_guess: Waiting takes precedence; after all waiting points are resolved, the run becomes `failed` if a failed node remains.

open_points.subject: Cancelling a run with an unknown effect outcome
open_points.text: “only the owner's resolution moves it: applied, or not applied” / “cancel a run | owner | the run ends `cancelled`; nothing further is sent | a finished run cannot be cancelled”
open_points.question: May the owner cancel a run while an EffectAttempt is `unknown`, leaving that attempt permanently unresolved?
options: Allow cancellation and retain the unresolved `unknown` attempt
Refuse cancellation until every unknown outcome is resolved
Cancel the run and require the owner to resolve the attempt independently afterward
open_points.default_guess: Allow cancellation and retain the attempt as `unknown`, because the cancel action excludes only finished runs and resolution is forbidden after the run ends.

open_points.subject: TrialCase expected outputs
open_points.text: “`expected_outputs`: StoredValues by output port, a `many` file port as a list like `inputs`, absent when only the absence of failure is required”
open_points.question: When `expected_outputs` is present, must it contain every contract output port, or may an authored trial case assert only a subset of outputs?
options: It must contain every output port
It may contain any subset of output ports
It may omit only designated optional output ports
open_points.default_guess: Require all output ports when `expected_outputs` is present; absence of the whole field means validation without equality expectations.
